_comment: Screenshot manifest for docs/screenshots.md and the README.
Each entry records the route, theme, viewport and the demo data it needs, so
the set can be regenerated without guesswork. Capture with:
Themes are switched through the application's own toggle, not injected CSS.

screenshots.name: client-dashboard-light
screenshots.heading: Client dashboard
screenshots.caption: Open a client and see the week ahead: scheduled tickets, maintenance falling due, monitor status, and where their sites are.
screenshots.alt: Client dashboard for Northwind Logistics in light theme: the navigation bar with the selected client, quick actions, record counts, the next seven days of scheduled work, outstanding tasks with due badges, monitor status and a site map

screenshots.name: my-work-light
screenshots.heading: My Work
screenshots.caption: Everything waiting on one technician: a running timer with a stop button, open tickets in SLA order, tickets where the customer has replied, the waiting-on-us and waiting-on-customer queues, pending approvals and the week's appointments. Each count matches the list its link opens.
screenshots.alt: My Work page in light theme: a running timer, eleven open tickets sorted by SLA due time, upcoming appointments, and pending approvals for an expense, three timesheets, change votes and invoices on hold

screenshots.name: global-dashboard-dark
screenshots.heading: Every client at once
screenshots.caption: The MSP-wide view: totals across all tenants, thirty-day health, and a map of every client site.
screenshots.alt: Cross-tenant dashboard in dark theme showing counts for organizations, users, assets, documents and monitors, a thirty-day health summary, and a map of client sites across the United States

screenshots.name: client-overview-light
screenshots.heading: Customer overview
screenshots.caption: Everything about one customer in one place — contacts, sites, and shortcuts into their documentation.
screenshots.alt: Customer overview page in light theme showing company information, primary contact details and two mapped sites

screenshots.name: project-timeline-light
screenshots.heading: Project timeline
screenshots.caption: Drag a bar to reschedule. Dependencies show what is blocked and what it is waiting for.
screenshots.alt: Project timeline in light theme: a Gantt chart of seven tasks with milestones marked, above a dependency table showing blocked tasks and what each waits for

screenshots.name: dispatch-board-dark
screenshots.heading: Dispatch board
screenshots.caption: A week of work per technician. Drag a ticket onto a row to schedule it; the banner flags anything close to breaching.
screenshots.alt: Dispatch board in dark theme showing a week of scheduled work by technician with an SLA-at-risk banner and unassigned tickets

screenshots.name: report-profitability-light
screenshots.heading: Profitability by client
screenshots.caption: Revenue against cost of delivery for the period, drawn from logged time and issued invoices — not typed in.
screenshots.alt: Profitability by client report in light theme showing revenue, cost, margin and blended margin percentage with a per-client breakdown

screenshots.name: report-client-health-dark
screenshots.heading: Client health score
screenshots.caption: A composite of SLA performance, ticket velocity, billing aging and engagement — so at-risk accounts surface before they churn.
screenshots.alt: Client health score report in dark theme ranking five clients by a composite score built from SLA, velocity, aging, engagement and an NPS proxy

screenshots.name: report-hourly-rate-light
screenshots.heading: Effective hourly rate
screenshots.caption: What an hour actually earned once non-billable time is counted, per client and per technician.
screenshots.alt: Effective hourly rate report in light theme showing average, highest, lowest and median rates with billable hours and utilisation per client

screenshots.name: rack-elevation-dark
screenshots.heading: Rack elevation
screenshots.caption: Each device is drawn from the same catalog artwork as its device page, across its real unit span — a 2U server reads as one 2U chassis. Front and rear faces, half-depth rules, and a plain face where no artwork is recorded.
screenshots.alt: Rack elevation in dark theme drawn from catalog artwork: a FortiGate firewall at U40, an HPE Aruba 6300M core switch at U37, a 2U Panduit patch panel, a legacy KVM console placement with no model shown as a plain face with its saved name, Dell PowerEdge R650 and 2U R750xs servers and a 2U Synology NAS, each named beside the rack with its model and units

screenshots.name: ipam-subnets-light
screenshots.heading: IP address management
screenshots.caption: Subnets per client with their VLAN, gateway and DNS, and which addresses are allocated, reserved or free.
screenshots.alt: IP address management in light theme listing four subnets with network, VLAN, gateway and location for one client

screenshots.name: scheduling-dark
screenshots.heading: Recurring maintenance
screenshots.caption: Maintenance that recurs on its own schedule, with per-task sign-off, kept separate from the ticket queue.
screenshots.alt: Scheduling page in dark theme showing tasks needing sign-off and upcoming maintenance for the next seven days with priority and status

screenshots.name: monitors-light
screenshots.heading: Uptime and certificate expiry
screenshots.caption: Endpoint checks with response time, and the certificate expiry date you would otherwise find out about at 2am.
screenshots.alt: Website monitor list in light theme showing monitored endpoints with status, response time, SSL expiry date and last check time

screenshots.name: ticket-queue-dark
screenshots.heading: Service desk queue
screenshots.caption: Every client in one queue. Filter by status, priority, queue or technician; the subject is what you scan, not the badges.
screenshots.alt: Service desk queue in dark theme listing 36 tickets across five clients with subject and ticket number, client, priority, status, queue, assignee, a Needs reply flag, last activity with who acted, and age

screenshots.name: ticket-detail-light
screenshots.heading: A ticket that knows the customer
screenshots.caption: The ticket reads as a conversation: the customer on the left, technicians on the right, internal notes in amber marked staff only, and status changes as compact rows. Contract hours, the SLA countdown and the credentials this job needs sit alongside — listed, never revealed.
screenshots.alt: Ticket detail in light theme laid out as a conversation: customer messages in left-hand bubbles labelled Customer, technician replies in blue right-hand bubbles labelled Technician, an amber internal note marked staff only, a status-change row and a composer set to Public reply, beside the Cc list, the active contract, problem link, closeout checklist, details and the asset card

screenshots.name: ticket-composer-dark
screenshots.heading: Internal note composer
screenshots.caption: Public reply and internal note are separate modes. An internal note gets an amber composer that says it is never sent to the client, and an unsent reply is saved as a draft only its author can see.
screenshots.alt: Ticket reply composer in dark theme switched to Internal note, with an amber box labelled staff only and a restored draft

screenshots.name: documents-dark
screenshots.heading: Client documentation
screenshots.caption: Per-client documents and global knowledge base articles, searchable by title and body.
screenshots.alt: Document list in dark theme showing per-client documentation with category, tags and last-updated date

screenshots.name: kb-runbook-light
screenshots.heading: Runbooks beside the work
screenshots.caption: A procedure written for the technician who will actually run it — and linked from the tickets that need it.
screenshots.alt: Knowledge base runbook in light theme with when-to-use guidance, numbered steps and an escalation note

screenshots.name: assets-dark
screenshots.heading: Asset register
screenshots.caption: Every device you look after for a client, filterable by type, manufacturer, status and location.
screenshots.alt: Asset list in dark theme showing devices with name, type, manufacturer, model and serial number, with filters above

screenshots.name: asset-detail-light
screenshots.heading: Asset detail
screenshots.caption: Identity, network, operating system, hardware, rack position, warranty and lifecycle on one record.
screenshots.alt: Asset detail in light theme for a domain controller showing identity, network, operating system, hardware specification, physical position, lifecycle dates and tags

screenshots.name: vault-dark
screenshots.heading: Credential vault
screenshots.caption: AES-GCM encrypted at rest, organised per client. Secrets are never rendered into a list — opening one is a permissioned, audited act.
screenshots.alt: Password vault in dark theme listing nine credentials for one client with title, username and security status, every secret hidden

screenshots.name: quote-detail-light
screenshots.heading: Quote to signature
screenshots.caption: Line items, tax and total, a PDF, and a signing link the customer can use without an account. Accepting it can open a ticket or spin up a project.
screenshots.alt: Quote detail in light theme with line items, subtotal, tax and total, plus actions to view the PDF, email it, copy a signing URL or accept it

screenshots.name: invoice-detail-dark
screenshots.heading: Invoices that explain themselves
screenshots.caption: Every line carries its origin — a contract period, a logged time entry, an expense — so a billing query is answerable without reconstructing it.
screenshots.alt: Invoice detail in dark theme with line items tagged by origin, a payment recording form and a push-to-accounting action

screenshots.name: contract-detail-light
screenshots.heading: Agreements and hours
screenshots.caption: Block hours with rollover rules, auto-renewal, and a profitability snapshot for the current period.
screenshots.alt: Contract detail in light theme showing hours consumed, rollover policy, auto-renewal state and a profitability snapshot

screenshots.name: project-detail-dark
screenshots.heading: Project delivery
screenshots.caption: Tasks, milestones and assignees with budget consumption and profitability rolled up from the work already logged.
screenshots.alt: Project detail in dark theme showing client, owner, dates, a ready-to-bill panel, profitability, budget consumption and a task list with milestones

screenshots.name: quotes-list-light
screenshots.heading: Quote pipeline
screenshots.caption: Draft, sent and accepted quotes across every client, with totals and a one-click PDF.
screenshots.alt: Quote list in light theme showing three quotes across three clients with status, total and creation date

screenshots.name: invoices-list-dark
screenshots.heading: Billing at a glance
screenshots.caption: Sent, paid and overdue invoices with balances, and whether each has been pushed to your accounting system.
screenshots.alt: Invoice list in dark theme showing three invoices with sent, paid and overdue status, totals, balances and accounting push state

screenshots.name: contracts-list-light
screenshots.heading: Agreements per client
screenshots.caption: Which clients are on managed agreements, which are on block hours, and how much of the allowance is gone.
screenshots.alt: Contract list in light theme showing three agreements with type, status, hours used against allowance and period

screenshots.name: organizations-dark
screenshots.heading: Tenants and access
screenshots.caption: Every client is its own tenant. Membership decides who sees what; switching client context is one click.
screenshots.alt: Organization list in dark theme showing client tenants with member counts, asset counts and status

screenshots.name: feature-toggles-light
screenshots.heading: Feature toggles
screenshots.caption: The service desk, AI assistance and other modules are opt-in — off until an administrator turns them on.
screenshots.alt: Feature toggle settings in light theme showing switches for optional modules including the native PSA service desk

screenshots.name: compliance-overview-dark
screenshots.heading: Compliance frameworks per client
screenshots.caption: Which frameworks a client is enrolled in, how far through the attestation they are, and when recertification is next due.
screenshots.alt: Compliance overview in dark theme showing PCI-DSS and HIPAA framework cards for one client with progress bars, status counts and a recertification countdown

screenshots.name: compliance-checklist-light
screenshots.heading: Attestation checklist
screenshots.caption: Per-control status, notes and an evidence link, with who last reviewed it and when — the record you hand an auditor.
screenshots.alt: PCI-DSS attestation checklist in light theme with per-control status dropdowns, notes, evidence links and last-reviewed stamps, colour-coded by compliance state

screenshots.name: readiness-overview-light
screenshots.heading: Documentation readiness
screenshots.caption: Each customer scored against the documentation standards in force, worst first, with a count of unmet requirements.
screenshots.alt: Documentation readiness overview in light theme listing customers with readiness scores and unmet requirement counts

screenshots.name: readiness-customer-dark
screenshots.heading: Readiness for one customer
screenshots.caption: Every requirement in a standard, met or unmet, with a plain explanation of what is missing, why it matters, the records that satisfy it and a link to fix it.
screenshots.alt: Readiness page for one customer in dark theme showing a Microsoft 365 documentation standard with met and unmet requirements and fix buttons

screenshots.name: readiness-repair-light
screenshots.heading: Readiness repair queue
screenshots.caption: Everything unmet across customers in one list, filterable by customer, standard and owner. Excepted items are left out.
screenshots.alt: Readiness repair queue in light theme listing unmet requirements per customer with what is missing, the owner and a fix action

screenshots.name: portal-request-form-light
screenshots.heading: Request a service (customer portal)
screenshots.caption: A customer fills in a guided form from the service catalog. Questions can appear only when relevant (the laptop type appears once "Needs a laptop" is ticked), and the side panel says how long it usually takes and whether approval is needed.
screenshots.alt: Customer portal Employee onboarding request form in light theme with filled-in fields, a conditional laptop type question and a what-to-expect panel

screenshots.name: document-version-diff-dark
screenshots.heading: Document version compare
screenshots.caption: Compare any stored version of a document with the current one, line by line, and restore it if needed. A restore is audited and keeps the replaced content as a version.
screenshots.alt: Document version comparison in dark theme showing removed and added lines between version 1 and the current runbook, with a restore button

screenshots.name: kb-analytics-light
screenshots.heading: KB analytics
screenshots.caption: Most viewed and never viewed articles, articles past their review date with their owner, and searches that found nothing. Only zero-result searches are kept, for 90 days, and vault searches are never recorded.
screenshots.alt: KB analytics page in light theme with most viewed, past review date and never viewed tables and a list of top zero-result searches

screenshots.name: settings-scheduler-dark
screenshots.heading: Scheduler
screenshots.caption: The built-in scheduler's periodic jobs with their interval, last and next run, status and run count. A job that reports a problem shows its error here, such as recurring invoicing skipping a contract that is more than one period behind. Late fees are off until you turn them on.
screenshots.alt: Task scheduler settings in dark theme listing periodic jobs with run history, one failed recurring-invoice job showing its error message, and late fees switched off
screenshots.selector: tr:has-text("more than one billing period behind")

screenshots.name: settings-security-light
screenshots.heading: Security settings
screenshots.caption: Session limits, 2FA, password rules and lockout are set here and take effect when saved. A value fixed by an environment variable is marked "Set by environment" and can only be changed on the server.
screenshots.alt: Security settings page in light theme with session, 2FA, password policy and brute-force fields, two of them marked Set by environment

screenshots.name: hardware-device-light
screenshots.heading: A switch and its ports
screenshots.caption: A Dell PowerConnect 3448P drawn from its catalog layout, front and rear, with the VLAN overlay on. Click a port to document it; badges say which face was checked against the manufacturer's documentation and which is approximate.
screenshots.alt: Device page in light theme for a 48-port Dell PowerConnect 3448P switch: front and rear panel artwork with ports coloured by VLAN, a verified-front and approximate-rear badge, a VLAN legend and the port table below

screenshots.name: hardware-port-editor-dark
screenshots.heading: Port editor
screenshots.caption: Click a port on the artwork to edit it: description, technician label, admin state, speed, mode, native, tagged and voice VLANs, LAG and PoE. The cable and its far end are shown in the same panel. Operational state stays "Not observed" because nothing here polls the switch.
screenshots.alt: Switch page in dark theme with the port editor open for port 1/e12: description, mode access, VLAN 10 Staff with voice VLAN 20, PoE auto, and cable C-0012 to PP-01 Port 12, with the port highlighted on the panel artwork

screenshots.name: hardware-trace-light
screenshots.heading: Full cable trace
screenshots.caption: From one switch port to the workstation it serves: patch cable, panel front and rear, the permanent link in the wall, the jack and the last patch cable, with each cable's ID, type, colour and length.
screenshots.alt: Cable trace in light theme from switch port 12 through a patch panel, a 34.5 m permanent link and wall jack Office 104 A to workstation XYZ-WS-104, marked complete documented path

screenshots.name: hardware-panel-device-dark
screenshots.heading: Patch panel, front and rear
screenshots.caption: A 48-port panel with the connected overlay on. Port 12 and port 24 are cabled at the front and rear, while port 13 has only its permanent link at the rear. The overlay shows documented cables, not link state.
screenshots.alt: Patch panel PP-01 in dark theme with front and rear artwork, the connected overlay marking ports 12 and 24 cabled on both faces and port 13 cabled only at the rear

screenshots.name: hardware-panel-mapping-light
screenshots.heading: Front-to-rear port mapping
screenshots.caption: Each panel port as one row: what is patched into the front, which rear termination it maps to, the permanent link, and the device at the far end. A path that stops short is marked incomplete. "In use only" hides the empty ports.
screenshots.alt: Patch panel mapping in light theme for PP-01: port 12 from switch port 12 through C-0012 and L-104A to XYZ-WS-104 (complete), port 13 through L-105A to Office 105 jack A (incomplete), port 24 to XYZ-AP-01 (complete)

screenshots.name: hardware-cables-dark
screenshots.heading: Cable register
screenshots.caption: Every documented cable with both ends, type, colour, length and status. Select several to print their labels in one go.
screenshots.alt: Cable list in dark theme with nine cables: patch cables, permanent links and work-area cables with both ends, type, colour, length and installed status

screenshots.name: hardware-server-dark
screenshots.heading: A server with a module
screenshots.caption: A Dell PowerEdge R640 from the community library, with a two-port 10 GbE NIC installed in a PCIe bay. The module's ports join the device's port list and can be cabled like any other.
screenshots.alt: Device page in dark theme for a Dell PowerEdge R640 with rear artwork showing an installed two-port SFP NIC, approximate-layout badges and a port table including the module ports

screenshots.name: hardware-ap-light
screenshots.heading: Access point, top and bottom
screenshots.caption: A ceiling access point drawn from above and below. The uplink port is on the bottom face and is documented as a trunk with native VLAN 99 and tagged 10 and 30.
screenshots.alt: Access point page in light theme for a Ubiquiti U6 Pro with top and bottom artwork, the RJ45 uplink cabled on the bottom face, and the port row showing trunk VLANs 99 native, 10 and 30 tagged

screenshots.name: hardware-asset-artwork-light
screenshots.heading: Artwork on the asset record
screenshots.caption: The asset page shows the same generated front and rear artwork, with its accuracy badges and a link to the ports and cabling.
screenshots.alt: Asset detail page in light theme for XYZ-SW-01 with an illustration card showing the switch front and rear panels, accuracy badges and a ports and cabling button

screenshots.name: hardware-rack-dark
screenshots.heading: Rack from catalog artwork
screenshots.caption: Front and rear of a rack, drawn from each model's artwork at its U position. A half-depth device mounted at the front is outlined on the rear. Each face exports to SVG, PNG or PDF.
screenshots.alt: Rack elevation in dark theme with a patch panel, switch and firewall shown on the front and rear faces, the half-depth firewall outlined on the rear, and SVG, PNG and PDF export links

screenshots.name: hardware-connectivity-dark
screenshots.heading: Connectivity diagram
screenshots.caption: Drawn only from documented cables. Edges are labelled with the ports at each end, and a device whose path continues without a documented cable is outlined in red. Drag to arrange, save the layout, export it.
screenshots.alt: Physical connectivity diagram in dark theme: firewall, switch, patch panel, server, wall jacks, access point and workstation joined by labelled cables, two nodes flagged with undocumented continuations

screenshots.name: hardware-vlan-light
screenshots.heading: VLAN diagram
screenshots.caption: Which devices carry which VLANs, from the port configuration: solid lines for native or untagged, dashed for tagged or voice, with untagged/tagged/voice port counts on each line.
screenshots.alt: VLAN diagram in light theme linking VLANs 10 Staff, 20 Voice, 30 Guest and 99 Management to a firewall, switch, access point and workstation, with untagged, tagged and voice port counts

screenshots.name: hardware-catalog-light
screenshots.heading: Hardware catalog
screenshots.caption: About 16,500 device, module and rack models imported from the community device-type library at a pinned revision, each with generated artwork. Filter by manufacturer, kind, category or layout accuracy.
screenshots.alt: Hardware catalog in light theme showing 16,526 models as cards with panel thumbnails, inferred categories and approximate-layout badges, with manufacturer, kind, category and accuracy filters

screenshots.name: hardware-model-dark
screenshots.heading: A catalog model and its sources
screenshots.caption: Every model shows its artwork, its components and where they came from. This switch was entered from Dell's user guide: the page cites the pages used and says what the guide does not state.
screenshots.alt: Catalog model page in dark theme for the Dell PowerConnect 3448P with front and rear artwork, a component table and a source and provenance panel quoting the manufacturer's guide

screenshots.name: hardware-layout-editor-dark
screenshots.heading: Layout editor
screenshots.caption: Place, number and arrange a model's components in millimetres and save a new layout version. A face can only be marked verified with the document it was checked against.
screenshots.alt: Layout editor in dark theme for the PowerConnect 3448P front face, 48 ports in blocks of six, with arrange, numbering and label-position controls and a source document field

screenshots.name: hardware-labels-light
screenshots.heading: Labels
screenshots.caption: Device, rack, port, panel, wall-jack and cable labels from millimetre templates, printed at true size. Cable labels come in pairs, each end naming where the other goes, and a calibration page checks the printer.
screenshots.alt: Label page in light theme with label kind, a 38 × 19 mm cable-flag template, a list of cables to label and a print calibration link

screenshots.name: ticket-conversation-dark
screenshots.heading: A ticket conversation with Cc and a secure message
screenshots.caption: A customer's e-mailed request as a thread: replies quote what they answer, the internal note stays amber and staff-only, and the reply that carried a temporary password shows only the secure message's state — opened by the recipient — never its content. The header says what happened last and the Cc card lists who is copied on e-mailed replies.
screenshots.alt: Resolved ticket in dark theme titled Outlook keeps asking for my password: customer bubbles from Dana Whitfield on the left, technician replies from Jordan Reyes on the right with one showing Cc office.manager@northwind.example, an amber internal note marked staff only, status-change rows, and a dashed Secure message box reading opened by the recipient, opens once, its content encrypted and not shown; beside it a Copied on replies (Cc) card, the active contract and a linked known-error problem record

screenshots.name: ticket-cc-reply-light
screenshots.heading: Replying with Cc
screenshots.caption: Tick "Email this reply" and the Cc field appears, filled from the people the customer copied. The reply above it carried a first-day password as a secure message: sent by e-mail, not opened yet, opens once, with its expiry.
screenshots.alt: Ticket composer in light theme with Email this reply ticked and a Cc field pre-filled with hr@ridgeline.example and it.lead@ridgeline.example, below a technician reply whose dashed Secure message box reads sent by e-mail, not opened yet, opens once, with an expiry date

screenshots.name: ticket-secure-compose-dark
screenshots.heading: Adding a secure message
screenshots.caption: A secret such as a temporary password goes in its own box, not the reply. It is stored encrypted as a one-time link that only the requester receives, expires after 1, 3 or 7 days, and cannot be combined with Cc.
screenshots.alt: Public reply composer in dark theme with the Add a secure message section open: a box for the secret that goes only to marcus.bell@northwind.example, an Expires after 3 days selector, a Can be opened once checkbox, the note Can't be combined with Cc, and Email this reply ticked

screenshots.name: portal-ticket-light
screenshots.heading: The same ticket in the customer portal
screenshots.caption: The customer sees the shared conversation in the same layout, with no internal note and no technician working data. Where a reply carried a secure message, the portal says it went to their e-mail address as a separate link.
screenshots.alt: Customer portal ticket page in light theme for Northwind Logistics: a Received, In progress, Resolved progress bar, then the conversation with customer and technician bubbles, the Cc line on a reply, and a Secure message box reading sent to your e-mail address as a separate link that opens once, it has been opened; the internal note is absent

screenshots.name: portal-approvals-light
screenshots.heading: Approving a request as the named approver
screenshots.caption: A request type can name who approves it for each customer. Here Aaron is the named approver for access requests, so Dana's request waits on him and he gets Approve and Deny; other customer admins see who it is waiting on.
screenshots.alt: Customer portal Approvals page in light theme: an access request from Dana Whitfield for read and write access to the inventory share, labelled Approver: Aaron Lindqvist, with a comment box and Approve and Deny buttons

screenshots.name: rmm-pairing-form-light
screenshots.heading: Pairing an RMM for ticket integration
screenshots.caption: Any RMM that implements the ticket-rmm-v1 contract can be paired from its connection form: an integration key ID, two shared secrets, where requests are processed and an optional integration address. The connection must serve a single customer, and switching pairing on is a protected change that a second administrator approves.
screenshots.alt: Ticket integration pairing section of the Tactical RMM connection form in light theme, with the pairing switch, integration key ID, outbound and inbound secret fields, processing location and integration address

screenshots.name: rmm-pairing-status-dark
screenshots.heading: Pairing status on the connection
screenshots.caption: The connection page says in plain words whether the pairing is live, which tenant it is pinned to, what the RMM advertised in its last capabilities check and which read-only diagnostics it offers. If the RMM ever answers for a different tenant, the pairing stops.
screenshots.alt: Ticket integration pairing card in dark theme marked Paired: contract address, key ID, hosted processing, the pinned tenant beacon-ridgeline, the advertised capabilities, three read-only diagnostics, the time of the last check and a Check pairing button

screenshots.name: ticket-rmm-light
screenshots.heading: The ticket's asset and its paired RMM
screenshots.caption: A ticket names the asset it is about, chosen from that customer's assets only. Technicians see what the RMM last reported and, when the RMM is paired, the actions their Technician Access allows on that device: send the ticket, run a read-only diagnostic, open a view or control session, or refer a fix. Customers see none of it.
screenshots.alt: Asset card on a ticket in light theme for workstation RDG-OP3-PC: the RMM's online status and last check-in, then a Paired RMM block with Send to RMM, Request view and Request control buttons, a Disk space read-only diagnostic picker, Refer a fix, and three requests already sent: an approved fix referral, a completed diagnostic and a handoff with receipt confirmed

screenshots.name: rmm-handoff-preview-dark
screenshots.heading: Reviewing a handoff before it is sent
screenshots.caption: Send to RMM shows exactly what will leave: the destination, its tenant and device, and the redacted ticket context — the same evidence document ticket analysis uses, with what was left out and what was redacted. Nothing is sent until the technician confirms, and it counts as sent only when the RMM confirms receipt.
screenshots.alt: Send to RMM preview in dark theme for ticket PSA-2026-000036, naming Ridgeline — Tactical RMM, its integration address, tenant beacon-ridgeline and device RDG-OP3-PC, the four redacted items that would be sent, what was left out (one internal note), an optional note field and Send to RMM and Cancel buttons

screenshots.name: ticket-rmm-requests-dark
screenshots.heading: What the RMM said back
screenshots.caption: Every request keeps the RMM's signed status callbacks: a handoff counts as sent once receipt is confirmed, a read-only diagnostic's sanitised, size-limited result is shown to staff only, and a fix referral shows the RMM's approval. ClientSt0r only refers a fix; the RMM approves and runs it.
screenshots.alt: Requests to the RMM list on a ticket in dark theme: a handoff marked Sent with receipt confirmed, a Disk space diagnostic marked Completed with its staff-only result expanded showing C: at 4% free, and a fix referral to clear the X-ray bridge cache marked Approved in the RMM

screenshots.name: technician-access-rmm-light
screenshots.heading: Effective access with a paired RMM
screenshots.caption: The effective-access preview shows, for one technician at one customer, each capability's result and why. RMM, remote-access and fix capabilities stay Unavailable until the customer's paired RMM advertises them; remote sessions on the L2 preset are by request.
screenshots.alt: Preview effective access in light theme for demo.tech at Ridgeline Dental Group: ticket AI, Private RMM handoff, read-only diagnostics and low-risk fix requests allowed in scope; view and control sessions by time-limited request; advanced diagnostics, elevation, unattended access, clipboard and file transfer unavailable because the paired RMM does not advertise them; and locked rows such as approving an endpoint fix and running commands from ClientSt0r

screenshots.name: change-cab-dark
screenshots.heading: Change request and CAB vote
screenshots.caption: A change carries its implementation, rollback and impact plans, its window, and the CAB's votes. It can be implemented only once every required approver has approved and nobody has rejected it.
screenshots.alt: Change management page in dark theme for a high-risk firewall firmware upgrade marked Approved, ready to implement: implementation and rollback plans, impact assessment, scheduled window, and a CAB approval table with two approvals, a vote box and a Begin Implementation button

screenshots.name: problems-light
screenshots.heading: Problem records
screenshots.caption: Recurring incidents get a problem record of their own, from investigating to known error to resolved, with the tickets linked to it.
screenshots.alt: Problem Records list in light theme with problems such as VPN tunnels dropping on dead-peer-detection timeouts, recurring Outlook credential prompts and print spooler crashes, each with status, priority, assignee, linked tickets and created date

screenshots.name: catalog-approvers-dark
screenshots.heading: Named approvers per request type
screenshots.caption: For each customer a request type is offered to, staff pick which of that customer's people approve it. With nobody named, the customer's admins approve as before. Someone who has left is flagged and ignored, and nobody approves their own request.
screenshots.alt: Named approvers page in dark theme for the Access request type: a list of customers with how many approvers each has, and for Northwind Logistics a warning that Grace Holt is no longer an active person there and is ignored, with Aaron Lindqvist ticked among the customer's people and a Save approvers button

screenshots.name: crm-pipeline-dark
screenshots.heading: Sales pipeline
screenshots.caption: Opportunities by stage, each with its customer, value, probability and owner, and a weighted total per column. Drag a card to move it to another stage.
screenshots.alt: CRM sales pipeline in dark theme with Discovery, Qualified, Proposal, Negotiation, Closed Won and Closed Lost columns holding opportunities such as a managed security add-on and a server room refresh, with values, probabilities and weighted totals

screenshots.name: readiness-custom-fields-dark
screenshots.heading: Custom asset fields as requirements
screenshots.caption: A requirement can name your own custom asset fields. Here every server must record its vendor support contract and backup policy; the servers missing them are listed and the fix opens the asset's Custom Fields section.
screenshots.alt: Network baseline standard for Northwind Logistics in dark theme scoring 81.8 percent: four met requirements, and an unmet one, Servers have a support contract and backup policy, listing NWL-FS01 and NWL-NAS01 as missing Vendor support contract and Backup policy, with a Fill in the asset button

screenshots.name: readiness-prefill-light
screenshots.heading: A readiness fix opens a filled-in form
screenshots.caption: A readiness "Create it" link switches to the customer the gap belongs to and opens the form with what the requirement asks for already filled in. The form says which customer it saves in; nothing is saved until you click Save.
screenshots.alt: Create Document form in light theme opened from a readiness fix link, with a banner reading This will be saved in Northwind Logistics and the title already filled in

screenshots.name: status-page-light
screenshots.heading: Customer status page
screenshots.caption: A public status page per customer: only the services listed here appear, under a public name, and incidents are written for that audience rather than copied from tickets.
screenshots.alt: Status page editor in light theme for Northwind Logistics with a warning that the page is live and public, its link with a Rotate link control, two published services marked operational, and an ongoing VPN incident and a resolved website incident with update boxes

screenshots.name: tech-roster-light
screenshots.heading: Technician roster
screenshots.caption: Who is on shift now, with each technician's skills and certifications, and which certifications are expiring or have expired.
screenshots.alt: Tech Roster in light theme listing four technicians with on-shift or off-shift badges, skill and certification counts, and one expiring and one expired certification flagged

screenshots.name: secure-message-reveal-light
screenshots.heading: What the recipient of a secure message sees
screenshots.caption: A one-time link opens behind a button. Mail scanners and link previews fetch links without pressing it, so they no longer use up the message before the person it was sent to sees it.
screenshots.alt: Secure message page in light theme reading You have a secure message, it can be opened once, copy what you need before you leave the page, with its expiry time and a Show the message button

screenshots.name: security-features-light
screenshots.heading: Security Features
screenshots.caption: Every safeguard with what it protects, its default and what it needs — and, for the customer you pick, whether it is actually in effect there. Values fixed by an environment variable are named; a check that cannot be read shows Unknown, never On.
screenshots.alt: Security Features page in light theme with the effective state shown for Northwind Logistics: a Sign-in table listing two-factor sign-in, failed sign-in lockout, password rules and hashing, session time limits, the IP and country firewall and the Content Security Policy, each with a shipped badge, default and prerequisites, and its state at the customer such as Partly, On or Off, then a Client access table

screenshots.name: vault-visibility-dark
screenshots.heading: Vault visibility report
screenshots.caption: Technicians see a customer's vault entries only where a membership or their global role grants it. This read-only report shows which staff lost cross-customer visibility, what they still see and how many entries are now hidden. It grants nothing.
screenshots.alt: Vault Visibility report in dark theme explaining that vault titles stay inside the customers a technician is assigned to, with a table of technicians, the customers they still see, the customer they no longer see and the number of entries hidden

screenshots.name: technician-access-light
screenshots.heading: Technician Access
screenshots.caption: What each MSP technician may do with ticket AI and RMM tools, per customer, from L1, L2 and L3 presets. Narrowing applies at once; anything that widens access is a protected change that a different administrator approves.
screenshots.alt: Technician Access settings in light theme: the order of evaluation, a password and authenticator confirmation box, protected changes waiting, an effective-access preview, assignments of L1 Help Desk and L2 Technician presets to three technicians at Northwind Logistics, and the preset capability table

screenshots.name: superuser-approval-dark
screenshots.heading: Superuser Approval
screenshots.caption: Optional and off by default. When on, creating or promoting a superuser is a request that a different administrator must approve; until then the account is not a superuser. Turning the policy off is itself a protected change.
screenshots.alt: Superuser Approval page in dark theme with the policy turned on, two eligible administrators, and a grant of superuser to one account waiting for approval by a different administrator

screenshots.name: ticket-ai-models-dark
screenshots.heading: Ticket AI models (OPTIONAL AI)
screenshots.caption: Optional, off unless PSA AI is enabled. Model profiles name the provider, model and whose key it is; keys are write-only and sealed to the gateway. Each customer's AI policy decides what is allowed there.
screenshots.alt: Ticket AI Assist models and customer policies page in dark theme marked OPTIONAL AI, listing two model profiles with provider and model, a write-only stored key, MSP ownership for assigned customers only and enabled status, beside a New profile form

screenshots.name: security-incidents-dark
screenshots.heading: Security incidents
screenshots.caption: Alerts that need handling become incidents with a severity, a status, the client and asset involved, and the alerts behind them.
screenshots.alt: Security Incidents list in dark theme with VPN brute-force attempts, a compromised Microsoft 365 account and blocked ransomware incidents across three clients, each with severity, status, client, asset, opened time and alert count

screenshots.name: update-badge-light
screenshots.heading: Update available
screenshots.caption: When the scheduled update check finds a newer release, superusers see an Update badge in the top bar that links to Settings → Updates. Pages never contact GitHub while loading, and other users never see it.
screenshots.alt: Top navigation bar in light theme with an orange Update badge next to the search box
